title: Short-Term Functional Outcomes of Robot-Assisted Neurorehabilitation in a Heterogeneous Pediatric Neurological Cohort: A Real-World Case Series from Oman
content: Purpose: To describe short-term functional outcomes after a 4–6-week robot-assisted neurorehabilitation program in a heterogeneous, real-world pediatric neurological cohort in Oman. Methods: Retrospective case series of nine children (aged 2–14 years) treated at a dedicated pediatric robotic rehabilitation hospital in Muscat, Oman between June 2025 and January 2026. Children received individually tailored programs on a multi-device robotic and technology-assisted platform, in 45-minute sessions over 4 or 6 weeks. Motor, gait, and balance outcomes were extracted from routine clinical documentation (Berg Balance Scale, Gross Motor Function Measure, Function in Sitting Test, and narrative descriptors) and classified descriptively. Results: Six girls and three boys (mean age 7.8 years) were included: cerebral palsy (n = 4), genetic or metabolic conditions (n = 2), global developmental delay of undetermined etiology (n = 1), acquired brain injury (n = 1), and traumatic spinal cord injury (n = 1). Improvement was documented in 8 of 9 assessable children for motor function, 4 of 4 for gait, and 5 of 6 for balance. Conclusions: Robot-assisted neurorehabilitation delivered within a multimodal program was feasible and accompanied by favorable short-term functional change in this real-world Gulf cohort. Findings are descriptive; prospective studies with standardized reporting of device, dose, and outcomes are needed.
